answer_1.quote: We evaluate understanding of AAL by LLMs through production of language in each variety using automatic metrics and human judgments for two tasks: a counterpart generation task akin to dialect translation ... and a masked span prediction (MSP) task where models predict a phrase that was removed from their input...

answer_2.quote: We use both automatic and human evaluation metrics for the counterpart generation task. As with most generation tasks, we first measure n-gram overlap of the model generations and gold standard reference texts and in our experiments, we utilize the Rouge metric.

answer_4.quote: Human evaluation is also conducted on the generated counterparts. The same linguistics student, computer science student, and social work scientists involved in creating the dataset of aligned counterparts were also asked to judge model generations.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators were asked to rate each assigned counterpart using 5-point Likert scales on the dimensions below: Human-likeness (Human-like), Linguistic Match (Dialect), Meaning Preservation (Meaning), and Tone Preservation (Tone).
